newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Soy shipping conditions at key Brazilian ports.
newsitem.headline: Soy shipping conditions at key Brazilian ports.

text.p: Key Brazilian ports reported the following conditions for shipments of soybeans and soy products:

Vessels: Ocean Lady loading 47,000 tonnes soymeal. Lepetane loading 22,000 tonnes soymeal. Sun P loading 55,000 tonnes soybeans. Marine Ranger loading 54,000 tonnes soybeans. Humber loading 55,000 tonnes soybeans/meal. Vitastar waiting to dock, to load 54,500 tonnes soybeans. Stjepov waiting to dock, to load 27,000 tonnes soymeal. 16 vessels waiting to load soymeal, 12 to load soybeans and two load mixed cargoes (soymeal/corn and soybeans/meal).
Trucks: A total 1,459 trucks arrived on April 2, of which 1,079 trucks unloaded soybeans, 310 soymeal and 170 vegetable oils including soyoil.
Stocks: No figures available. NOTE: Stevedores at Paranagua may join a national strike on April 4 but have still not made a decision.

Vessels: Loading of most vessels was paralyzed due to a strike by stevedores which was scheduled to last until April 5. Huta Kotowice was docked at the port authority terminal to load 54,000 tonnes soybeans but was not operating. Aghia Trias was docked at the Cargill private terminal to load 59,126 tonnes soybeans but also not operating. Hilon of Sparta waiting to dock to load 55,000 soybeans.
Road: 459 trucks arrived on April 2 unloading 11,892 tonnes soybeans and 20 trucks arrived unloading 495 tonnes soymeal.
Rail: 121 wagons arrived unloading 6,884 tonnes soymeal and 25 wagons arrived unloading 1,332 tonnes soymeal.
